newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian youth march against Nobel laureate Belo.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian youth march against Nobel laureate Belo.

text.p: More than 2,000 members of the youth wing of Indonesia's ruling Golkar party demonstrated in Jakarta on Tuesday against East Timorese Nobel peace laureate Bishop Carlos Belo, demanding he be thrown out of the country.
Eyewitnesses said the youths, dressed in yellow uniforms, carried banners outside parliament saying "Expel Belo".

Newspaper reports said Belo was due appear before a parliamentary commission on Tuesday to answer questions about an interview with the German news magazine Der Spiegel in which he was reported to have said Indonesian troops had trampled on East Timor's independence "and treated us like dogs".
Church sources said the Roman Catholic bishop had flown from the East Timor capital of Dili on Monday and was attending an annual bishops' meeting in Jakarta on Tuesday.

Belo, jointly awarded the Nobel Peace Prize last month with self-exiled East Timorese-born activist Jose Ramos-Horta, has said he wanted to see the full text of the Der Spiegel interview before he commented further.

Residents in Dili said students at the University of East Timor were staging a protest outside the campus on Tuesday, the fifth anniversary of the killing of at least 50 demonstrators by Indonesian troops in the East Timorese capital.
Sources in close contact with East Timor said the protest was apparently partly in response to an attack on Belo in an Indonesian language newspaper reprinted in the local paper.

Belo, regarded as possibly the most influential civilian figure in East Timor, called recently for an end to violence and demonstrations in the former Portuguese colony occupied by Indonesian troops in December 1975.
Indonesian incorporated East Timor as its 27th province the following July.
